drills.title: Units per region, A-Z
drills.prompt: Arrange the lines so the program adds up the units sold in each region and prints the regions in A-Z order. The two imports can swap places. Two lines do not belong.
lines: List<Sale> sales = List.of(new Sale("West", 2), new Sale("East", 1), new Sale("West", 5));
drills.explain: Read groupingBy aloud: group the sales by region, keep the keys A-Z in a TreeMap, and add up qty inside each group. summingInt gives an Integer per group, which is what the Map<String, Integer> expects. counting() would produce a Long and the line would not compile, and the method is called groupingBy, not groupBy.

drills.title: Average per category, and a joined list
drills.prompt: Fill the blanks so the program prints the average quantity per category (categories A-Z) and then the product names, sorted and joined with commas.
code: record Sale(String category, String product, int qty) {}
List<Sale> sales = List.of(new Sale("Home", "Lamp", 2), new Sale("Grocery", "Tea", 4),
drills.explain: The middle argument of groupingBy chooses the Map to build: TreeMap::new is a constructor reference that keeps the categories A-Z. averagingDouble (or averagingInt) gives a Double per group, while counting() gives a Long and summingInt an Integer, so neither fits Map<String, Double>. To glue strings together you collect them with Collectors.joining(", "); there is no Collectors.join.

drills.title: Top 2 when the totals tie
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
code: List<Sale> sales = List.of(new Sale("Tea", 3), new Sale("Rice", 5), new Sale("Tea", 4),
drills.explain: Tea adds up to 3 + 4 = 7, Rice to 5 + 2 = 7 and Lamp to 7, so all three totals tie. sorted(...) is stable: entries that compare as equal keep their incoming order, which is the TreeMap order (Lamp, Rice, Tea). limit(2) then keeps the first two. A top-N with ties needs a tie-breaker such as thenComparing(Map.Entry::getKey), otherwise the result depends on the map you started from.

drills.title: toMap meets a repeated key
drills.prompt: The program should print one price per product, but it crashes. Click the faulty line, then choose the fix.
code: List<Sale> sales = List.of(new Sale("Tea", 120), new Sale("Rice", 480), new Sale("Tea", 120));
fixed_code: List<Sale> sales = List.of(new Sale("Tea", 120), new Sale("Rice", 480), new Sale("Tea", 120));
drills.explain: Tea appears twice, and toMap does not know which of the two prices to keep, so it throws IllegalStateException: Duplicate key Tea. The third argument is a merge function that decides: (first, second) -> first keeps the first price. Spelling the key and value functions as lambdas, or switching to toUnmodifiableMap, still gives no merge function, so the crash stays. TreeMap::new is a map factory, not a merge function.

drills.title: Review the AI's regional report
drills.prompt: An AI assistant wrote this report. It compiles and runs, but tick the real problems (there are three).
code: record Sale(String region, String product, int qty, double price) {}
List<Sale> sales = List.of(new Sale("West", "Tea", 3, 120.55), new Sale("East", "Rice", 1, 480.25),

issues.text: Every order is rounded before it is added to its region total
issues.why: Each rounding error is kept and added up, so the totals can drift by a few paise. Add the exact revenue and round once at the end (for example with replaceAll on the finished map).

issues.text: groupingBy without TreeMap::new returns a HashMap, so the regions have no guaranteed order
issues.why: A report should list the regions in a fixed order. Pass TreeMap::new as the middle argument (as Day 25 does), otherwise the order depends on hashing and can look random.

issues.text: avgQty divides two ints, so the average is cut down to 2.0 instead of 2.25
issues.why: totalQty / sales.size() is whole-number division and the decimals are gone before the result reaches the double. Use mapToInt(...).average() or divide by (double) sales.size().

non_issues.text: counting() returns a Long, so Map<String, Long> is a mistake
non_issues.why: Long is exactly what counting() produces. Map<String, Integer> would be the compile error.

non_issues.text: sales.stream() is called more than once, so the second stream is already closed
non_issues.why: Only one Stream object cannot be reused. Every call to sales.stream() creates a fresh stream from the list.

non_issues.text: The record needs getRegion() style getters to be used with Sale::region
non_issues.why: A record creates accessors named after its fields (region(), qty()), and Sale::region refers to exactly that method.

drills.explain: In generated report code look for rounding inside the loop, maps whose order matters but is not chosen, and divisions of two ints. The Collectors themselves were used correctly here.
